Ask for their ROC license number, proof of insurance, how long they've been in business and who will do the work. Ask what the estimate includes, what warranty applies and how hidden damage will be handled. Also ask how they'll protect your property and clean up.
What are the red flags when hiring a roofer?

Red flags include no license, pressure to sign immediately, cash-only payment, large up-front payments and vague verbal estimates. Be cautious with door-to-door sellers after storms and anyone who offers to cover your insurance deductible. A legitimate roofer will give you time and a written estimate.
What is a storm chaser roofer?

A storm chaser is a contractor, often from out of state, who follows storms and goes door to door offering roof work. Some do poor work or leave before problems appear, making warranties hard to use. Verify any roofer's Arizona license and local address before hiring.
Should I get more than one roofing estimate?

Getting more than one estimate is reasonable for larger projects. It helps you understand the scope of work and fair pricing. Compare estimates on the same scope and materials so the comparison is meaningful.
Should my roofing agreement be in writing?

Yes, always get a written contract before work begins. It should describe the scope, materials, price, payment schedule, timeline and warranty information. A written agreement protects both you and the contractor.
What should I ask about roofing warranties?

Ask about both the manufacturer's material warranty and the contractor's workmanship warranty. Find out how long each lasts, what they cover, whether they transfer to a new owner and what could void them. Get warranty terms in writing.
Is it a red flag if a roofer offers to pay my insurance deductible?

Yes. Offering to cover or waive your deductible can amount to insurance fraud and may put you at risk. It can also signal that the contractor plans to inflate the claim. Avoid contractors who make this offer.
Should I hire a roofer who knocks on my door after a storm?

Be careful. Some door-to-door roofers are legitimate, but storm chasers often use this approach. Verify the license on roc.az.gov, ask for a local address and references, and don't sign anything on the spot.
Can a handyman repair my roof in Arizona?

Arizona has a limited handyman exemption for small jobs, generally under $1,000 including labor and materials and not requiring a permit. Roof work often goes beyond that, and a licensed roofer is accountable to the Registrar of Contractors. For anything more than a minor repair, hire a licensed roofing contractor.
How can I check a roofer's reputation?

Read online reviews, ask for references from recent local jobs and check the ROC website for complaints. Years in business and a local office are also good signs. Consistent feedback over time tells you more than a handful of reviews.
Why does hiring a local roofer matter?

A local roofer understands Valley weather, city requirements and common HOA rules. They're also nearby if you need warranty service or future repairs. Local roofers depend on their reputation in the community.
What does licensed, bonded and insured mean for a roofer?

Licensed means the contractor holds an active license from the Arizona Registrar of Contractors. Bonded means a surety bond is in place as required for the license. Insured means the contractor carries liability and workers' compensation coverage.
Should I ask a roofer for references?

Yes, asking for references from recent jobs in your area is a good idea. Ask past customers about communication, cleanup and how problems were handled. You can also drive by finished roofs to see the work.
What should I do if I have a problem with my roofer?

Contact the roofer first and explain the problem clearly, keeping notes and copies of any written communication. If it isn't resolved, you can file a complaint with the Arizona Registrar of Contractors. Keep your contract, payment records and photos.
Do roofing companies use subcontractors?

Some roofing companies use subcontractors and others use their own crews. Ask who will actually be working on your roof and whether they are licensed and insured. The contractor you hire should be responsible for the work either way.
How should I compare roofing bids side by side?

Compare the scope of work, roofing material, underlayment type, decking allowances, ventilation and flashing details. Check whether permits, disposal and cleanup are included. Then look at warranty terms and the contractor's license and insurance.

categories.title: HOA rules and permits
categories.intro: Architectural approvals, tile color rules and city permits in Gilbert, Mesa, Chandler and nearby cities.
faqs: Do I need HOA approval to replace my roof?

Many Arizona HOAs require architectural approval before a roof replacement, especially if the material or color will change. Some require approval even for a like-for-like replacement. Check your CC&Rs and design guidelines before scheduling work.
How do I get HOA approval for a new roof?

Contact your HOA or management company and request an architectural review application. You'll typically provide the roofing material, manufacturer, color name and sometimes a sample or photo. Your roofer can give you the product details you need.
How long does HOA roof approval take?

HOA approval can take anywhere from a few days to several weeks, depending on how often the architectural committee meets. Plan ahead, especially if you want to finish before monsoon season. Start the request as soon as you've chosen your roofing materials.
Can my HOA dictate the color of my roof tile?

Yes, many HOAs limit roof colors to an approved palette to keep a consistent look in the neighborhood. Your new tile may need to match the original or come from the approved list. Ask your HOA for its current options.
Will my HOA approve a substitute if my tile is discontinued?
If your original tile is discontinued, your HOA may approve a similar color from a current product line. Some communities have already approved replacements. Ask your HOA before ordering materials.
Do I need a permit to replace my roof in Gilbert, Mesa or Chandler?

Generally, yes. Roof replacements in Gilbert, Mesa, Chandler and most Valley cities require a building permit. Your licensed roofer typically pulls the permit, but confirm current requirements with the city.
Do roof repairs need a permit?

Small roof repairs usually don't require a permit, but larger repairs may, depending on the city and the size of the area involved. Each city sets its own thresholds. Check with your city or ask your roofer.
Who pulls the roofing permit, the homeowner or the roofer?

In most cases, the licensed roofing contractor pulls the permit for the job. That makes the contractor responsible for meeting code and passing inspections. Be wary of a contractor who asks you to pull the permit yourself.
What happens during a city roof inspection?

City inspectors check that the work meets building code, which may include the decking, underlayment and fastening before roofing goes on, plus a final inspection. Inspection timing varies by city and roof type. Passing inspections closes out the permit.
What happens if a roof is replaced without a permit?

Unpermitted roof work can cause problems when you sell your home, file an insurance claim or deal with the city. You may be required to get a permit after the fact or have work inspected or redone. Using a licensed roofer who pulls permits avoids these issues.
Can my HOA prevent me from installing solar panels?

Arizona law generally limits HOAs from prohibiting solar energy devices, though they may set reasonable rules about placement and appearance. Requirements vary by community. This isn't legal advice, so review your HOA documents and ask a professional if you have questions.
Does HOA approval replace the need for a city permit?
No, HOA approval and city permits are separate. The HOA reviews appearance and community standards, while the city enforces building codes. Most roof replacements need both.
Can my HOA require a specific roofing material?
Yes, many HOAs require specific materials, such as concrete or clay tile, for sloped roofs. Some also restrict tile profiles and colors. Review your design guidelines before choosing a new roof.
What information does an HOA usually need for roof approval?

HOAs commonly ask for the roofing material type, manufacturer, product line, color name and a sample or photo. Some also want the contractor's name and license number. Having this information ready can speed up approval.
Do I need to tell my neighbors before roof work?

It's not usually required, but it's considerate to let neighbors know about noise, dumpsters and trucks. Your HOA may have rules about work hours and where materials can be placed. A heads-up helps keep relations good.
Does my HOA have rules about work hours and dumpsters?

Many HOAs set rules for construction hours, dumpster placement and how long materials can sit in a driveway or on the street. Check your HOA's guidelines and share them with your roofer. Following the rules helps avoid violation notices.
Can my HOA require me to repair my roof?

Many HOA CC&Rs require homeowners to keep their homes in good repair, including visible roof damage. If damage is visible from the street, you may receive a notice. Check your CC&Rs for maintenance requirements.
Do building codes require specific underlayment for re-roofs?

Building codes set minimum requirements for underlayment, fastening and flashing, based on the code each city has adopted. Manufacturers may have additional requirements. Your roofer should install a system that meets both.
Are there roofing rules in Phoenix historic districts?

Homes in Phoenix historic districts may need historic preservation review before changes to the roof's appearance or materials. Requirements depend on the district and the project. Check with the City of Phoenix before planning work.
Do foam roof recoats or coatings need a permit?

A recoat or coating on an existing roof often doesn't require a permit, but a new foam roof or full replacement usually does. Requirements vary by city and scope. Confirm with your city or roofer before work begins.

categories.title: Insurance claims
categories.intro: General guidance on roof damage and homeowners insurance; this is not legal advice.
faqs: Does homeowners insurance cover roof damage?

Homeowners insurance often covers sudden, accidental roof damage, such as damage from wind, hail or a falling tree. It typically doesn't cover normal wear, aging or lack of maintenance. Read your policy and talk with your insurer about your specific coverage.
Does insurance pay for interior water damage from a roof leak?

It depends on what caused the leak. If a covered event such as wind damage let water in, the resulting interior damage may be covered, while leaks from aging or wear generally aren't. Your policy and insurer decide what's covered, so report the damage and ask.
How do I document roof damage for an insurance claim?

Take dated photos and video of the damage, including any debris, broken tiles or shingles on the ground and interior stains. Write down when the storm happened and what you noticed. Keep receipts for any temporary repairs or protection.
Should I call my roofer or my insurance company first?

Contact your insurer promptly to report the damage, since many policies have notice requirements. A roofer's inspection can help you understand the damage and the scope of repairs. You can do both quickly and in either order.
What does an insurance adjuster do?

An insurance adjuster inspects the damage on behalf of the insurance company and estimates what the policy will pay. They review the cause of damage and your coverage. Ask questions if anything in their report is unclear.
Can my roofer be there when the insurance adjuster inspects?
Many insurers allow a contractor to be present during the adjuster's inspection. A roofer can point out damage and explain what repairs involve. Ask your insurer if you'd like to arrange this.
What is the difference between actual cash value and replacement cost coverage?

Actual cash value coverage pays the value of the damaged roof minus depreciation for age and wear. Replacement cost coverage pays to repair or replace it with similar materials, though some policies hold back part of the payment until work is done. Your policy declarations show which coverage you have.
What is a roof insurance deductible?

A deductible is the amount you pay before insurance coverage applies. Some policies have separate deductibles for wind or hail, sometimes calculated as a percentage of the home's insured value. Check your policy to see which applies.
Will insurance replace my whole roof if only part is damaged?

Insurers typically pay to repair the damaged area, not the entire roof, unless the damage is widespread or repairs aren't practical. Matching issues with discontinued materials can affect the decision. Your policy and the adjuster's evaluation determine the outcome.
Can insurance deny a claim because my roof is old?

Insurers may deny or reduce claims if they believe damage was caused by age, wear or prior conditions rather than a covered event. Roof age also affects actual cash value payments. Inspection records and maintenance history can help show the roof's condition before the storm.
What should I do if my roof insurance claim is denied?

Read the denial letter to understand the reason, and ask your insurer to explain anything unclear. You can request a reinspection, provide additional documentation or appeal the decision. For complex disputes, consider talking with a licensed public adjuster or an attorney.
Should I make temporary roof repairs before the adjuster arrives?

Many policies expect you to take reasonable steps to prevent further damage, such as having a roof tarped. Photograph the damage first and keep receipts for any temporary work. Avoid permanent repairs until your insurer has had a chance to inspect, unless they tell you otherwise.
How long do I have to file a roof damage claim?

Deadlines for reporting damage and filing a claim depend on your policy. Some require prompt notice after damage occurs. Report damage as soon as you can and check your policy for specific time limits.
Will filing a roof claim raise my insurance premium?

It might, depending on your insurer, your claims history and the type of claim. Weather-related claims are sometimes treated differently from others. Ask your insurance agent how a claim could affect your premium.
Can my insurer non-renew my policy because of my roof's age?

Some insurers have guidelines about roof age or condition and may require an inspection, change coverage or decline to renew. Rules vary by company. Ask your agent about your insurer's requirements before renewal time.
What is a public adjuster?

A public adjuster is a licensed professional you can hire to represent you in an insurance claim. They usually charge a percentage of the claim payment. They can be helpful for large or disputed claims.
Can a roofer negotiate my insurance claim for me?

A roofer can document damage, provide a repair estimate and explain the scope of work. Negotiating a claim on your behalf is generally the role of a licensed public adjuster or attorney. This is general information, not legal advice.
What records help with a roof insurance claim?

Helpful records include your roof's installation date, past inspection reports, repair invoices and before-and-after photos. Storm dates and photos taken right after the damage are also useful. Keep these in one place so they're easy to find.
What is ordinance or law coverage for roofs?

Ordinance or law coverage helps pay the extra costs of bringing repairs up to current building codes. Without it, code-required upgrades may not be covered. Check your policy or ask your agent whether you have it.
Should I sign an assignment of benefits for my roof claim?

An assignment of benefits transfers some of your insurance claim rights to a contractor. Read any such agreement carefully and understand what you're giving up before signing. Consider getting legal advice, since this is not legal advice.

categories.title: Solar panels and your roof
categories.intro: Planning roof work around solar, and protecting your roof when panels go on.
faqs: Should I replace my roof before installing solar panels?

If your roof or its underlayment is close to the end of its life, it's usually wise to replace it before installing solar. Solar systems are designed to last many years, and removing panels later for roof work adds cost and time. A roof inspection before solar installation helps you decide.
What is a solar detach and reset?

A solar detach and reset is the process of removing solar panels so roof work can be done, then reinstalling them afterward. It's common during re-felts and roof replacements. The panels are disconnected, stored safely and reinstalled when the roof work is complete.
Who removes solar panels for roof work?

Solar panels should be removed and reinstalled by a qualified solar contractor. Check with your solar company first, since removal by others may affect its warranty. The roofer and solar contractor then coordinate timing.
Can solar panels cause roof leaks?

Yes, solar installations can lead to leaks if mounts aren't properly flashed or tiles were broken during installation. Each mounting point is a roof penetration. Having the roof checked after installation helps catch problems early.
How are solar panels mounted on tile roofs?

On tile roofs, solar mounts are typically attached through the decking with flashed mounts, and tiles at those points are modified or replaced. Some systems use replacement tile mounts designed to shed water. Careful installation protects both the tiles and the underlayment.
Can a roof be repaired under solar panels?

Small repairs near the edges of an array are sometimes possible, but access under panels is limited. Larger repairs, such as underlayment replacement, usually require removing the panels. A roofer can tell you what's needed after an inspection.
Why do pigeons nest under solar panels?

The shaded space under solar panels is sheltered and attractive to pigeons. Their nests and droppings can damage the roof, clog drainage and create a mess. Mesh critter guards around the array help keep birds out.
Do solar installations damage tile roofs?

Solar installation can crack tiles if installers walk on them or handle them carelessly. Broken tiles under or near panels may go unnoticed. Ask for broken tiles to be replaced and have the roof inspected after installation.
How much roof life should I have left before adding solar?

Ideally, your roof should have many years of life left before solar is installed. If the underlayment or roofing is likely to need replacement within the solar system's lifespan, consider doing the roof first. An inspection gives you a realistic estimate.
How are solar mounts sealed on a foam roof?
On foam roofs, solar is attached with properly sealed mounts or set on ballasted racking. Attachments need to be flashed and coated to keep water out. Plan any needed recoat before the panels go on.
Can solar panels be installed on a flat roof?

Yes, flat roofs often use tilted racks that are either attached to the roof or held down with ballast. Drainage paths and roof weight capacity need to be considered. Keeping the roof in good shape before installation is important.
Should I have my roof inspected after solar is installed?
Yes, an inspection after solar installation can catch broken tiles, unsealed penetrations or debris left behind. It's easier to fix these early. Keep the inspection report with your solar paperwork.
Do solar panels protect the roof underneath them?
Solar panels shade the roof underneath, which can reduce UV exposure. However, they also trap debris and give birds a place to nest. The roof under panels still needs periodic checks.
Does roof work affect my solar panel warranty?
It can. Some solar warranties require that only approved contractors remove or reinstall panels. Check your solar warranty and contact your solar company before scheduling roof work.
How much time does a solar detach and reset add to a roof project?

Detach and reset adds time because the solar company has to schedule removal and reinstallation around the roof work. Depending on their availability, this can add days or weeks. Plan early, especially before monsoon season.
Can you coordinate roof work with my solar company?

Yes, roof work around solar has to be timed with your solar company's removal and reinstallation. We'll plan the roofing work around when your solar contractor can take the panels down and put them back. Contact your solar company early to get on their schedule.
Do solar panels add weight to my roof?

Solar panels add weight, typically a few pounds per square foot, which most roofs can handle. The weight is spread across mounting points. Flat roofs with ballasted systems carry more weight and should be evaluated first.
Is the roof under solar panels replaced during a re-felt?

Yes, once the panels are removed, the roof under them gets the same new underlayment and tile work as the rest of the roof. This area often benefits because it's been hard to inspect. The panels go back on after the roofing is done.
Are solar panels covered in a roof insurance claim?

Solar panels attached to your home may be covered under your homeowners policy, depending on the policy. Leased systems may be covered by the leasing company instead. Tell your insurer about your solar system and ask how it's covered.
Should I climb on my roof to clean solar panels?

No, avoid climbing on the roof to clean panels, especially on tile. Rinse lightly from the ground if your solar company allows it, or hire a professional panel cleaner. Walking on the roof can break tiles and lead to falls.

categories.title: Commercial roofing
categories.intro: Roofing for offices, retail, industrial buildings, HOA facilities and multifamily properties.
faqs: What commercial roofing services does Integrity Roofing provide?

We provide commercial roof repairs, inspections, maintenance, foam roofing, recoats, elastomeric coatings, flat roofs and sloped commercial roofs. We work on tile and shingle roofs on commercial buildings as well. Call 602-548-3770 to talk about your property.
What roof systems are common on Arizona commercial buildings?

Commercial buildings in Arizona commonly use spray foam roofs, built-up roofs, modified bitumen and single-ply membranes, often with reflective coatings. Sloped commercial buildings may have tile or shingles. The right system depends on the building's structure, use and budget.
How often should a commercial roof be inspected?

Commercial roofs should be inspected at least twice a year, typically in spring and fall, and after major storms. Regular inspections catch drainage problems and damage early. They also help with budgeting and warranty requirements.
Can a commercial roof be recoated instead of replaced?

Yes, many commercial roofs can be recoated if the existing roof is dry and structurally sound. A moisture survey may be used to find wet areas that need replacement first. Recoating can extend the roof's life with less disruption to the building.
How do roof coatings help commercial buildings?

Reflective coatings lower roof surface temperatures, which can reduce cooling loads. They also protect the roof from UV and can extend its life. Coating projects often cause less disruption than tear-offs.
Can roofing work be done while my business is open?
In most cases, yes. Roofing work can often be scheduled around business hours, with attention to noise, odors, parking and safe access. Discuss your operations with your roofer during planning.
What causes most commercial roof leaks?

Common causes include rooftop equipment, failed flashing at penetrations, ponding water, clogged drains and parapet walls. Foot traffic from service technicians can also damage the roof. Regular maintenance targets these problem areas.
Why are rooftop HVAC units a common source of leaks?

HVAC units sit on curbs that need flashing, and condensate lines and drain pans can leak. Technicians walking to and from units can damage the roof surface. Inspecting around units during routine maintenance helps prevent leaks.
What is included in a commercial roof maintenance plan?

A maintenance plan typically includes scheduled inspections, clearing drains and scuppers, sealing small problems and documenting the roof's condition. It helps prevent leaks and plan for future work. We can set up regular maintenance visits for your property.
Who is responsible for roof repairs in a leased commercial building?
Responsibility depends on the lease. Some leases make the landlord responsible for the roof, while others pass maintenance to the tenant. Review your lease to see who handles repairs.
Does a commercial roofer need a different license in Arizona?

Yes, commercial roofing in Arizona requires a commercial roofing classification, such as C-42, or a dual classification such as CR-42. Residential-only licenses don't cover commercial work. Check the contractor's classification at roc.az.gov.
How long do commercial roofs last?

Commercial roof life depends on the system, installation and maintenance. Coated and foam roofs can last a long time when recoated on schedule, while other systems vary. Regular inspections help you get the full life from your roof.
Can a commercial roof be replaced in phases?

Yes, large commercial roofs can sometimes be replaced or recoated in phases to spread out costs and limit disruption. The phases must be planned so each section ties in properly. An inspection helps decide which areas need attention first.
What is tapered insulation on a flat roof?
Tapered insulation is insulation board cut at a slight slope to direct water toward drains or scuppers. It's used to improve drainage on flat roofs. It also adds insulation value to the roof.
How should I budget for a commercial roof replacement?

Start with a professional inspection to estimate remaining roof life and identify needed repairs. Use that information to plan capital expenses over several years. Every roof is different, so see our Roofing Cost Guide at /resources/roofing-cost-guide/ for cost factors.
Do HOA clubhouses and multifamily buildings count as commercial roofing?
Often, yes. HOA facilities, apartment buildings and multifamily properties are usually handled as commercial projects. Requirements depend on the building and city codes.
What roofing documents should property managers keep?

Property managers should keep inspection reports, photos, repair invoices, warranties and contractor insurance certificates. These records help with budgeting, insurance and warranty claims. They also make it easier to brief new owners or managers.
What safety rules apply to commercial roof work?

Commercial roof work must follow fall protection and other workplace safety rules. Roof access points, edges and skylights need special attention. Property managers should limit roof access to trained personnel.
How can disruption to tenants be kept to a minimum during roof work?

Give tenants advance notice, schedule noisy work at appropriate times and plan parking and access around the project. Keep a clear point of contact for questions. Good communication prevents most complaints.
Can skylights on commercial roofs be a hazard?

Yes, skylights can be a fall hazard because they may not support a person's weight. They should be protected with screens or guards when people work nearby. Skylights also need regular checks for leaks around their curbs.

categories.title: Gutters, flashing, ventilation, skylights and roof components
categories.intro: The parts of a roof that keep water moving the right direction.
faqs: What is roof flashing?

Flashing is metal or membrane material installed where the roof meets walls, chimneys, vents, skylights and valleys. It directs water away from joints that would otherwise leak. Flashing failures are one of the most common causes of roof leaks.
Where does roof flashing usually fail?

Flashing often fails where the roof meets a wall, around chimneys and skylights, in valleys and around pipes. Sun, heat cycles and movement loosen it over time. Sealant at flashing edges also breaks down.
What is a pipe boot on a roof?

A pipe boot, also called a pipe jack, is a flashing piece that seals around plumbing vent pipes. Many have rubber collars that crack in Arizona sun. Cracked boots are a common and fixable leak source.
What is counter flashing?

Counter flashing is a piece of flashing that overlaps the base flashing where the roof meets a wall or chimney. It sheds water over the top of the base flashing. It's often tucked into stucco or masonry.
What is step flashing?

Step flashing is a series of small, bent flashing pieces installed along the side of a wall where it meets a sloped roof. Each piece overlaps the one below, layered with the roofing. It helps direct water away from the wall joint.
What is a roof cricket?

A cricket is a small, peaked structure built behind a chimney or other obstruction to divert water around it. Without one, water can pool and leak. Crickets are also used on flat roofs to direct water toward drains.
What are soffits and fascia?
Soffits are the panels under the roof overhang, and fascia is the board along the roof edge. Soffits often contain vents for attic airflow. Fascia supports gutters and protects the roof edge.
Why does fascia rot or peel?

Fascia rots when water gets behind gutters or flashing and soaks the wood. In Arizona, sun also breaks down paint quickly, exposing wood to moisture. Keeping paint and drip edge in good shape protects it.
Do Arizona homes need gutters?

Many Arizona homes don't have gutters, but they can be useful. Gutters help protect entryways, patios, foundations and landscaping from roof runoff. They're especially helpful where runoff causes erosion or splashes against walls.
What size gutters work best in Arizona?

Five-inch gutters are common on homes, while six-inch gutters handle more water from large roofs or steep slopes. Monsoon downpours can overwhelm undersized gutters. Downspout size and placement matter as much as gutter size.
Why do gutters overflow during monsoon storms?

Gutters overflow when they're clogged with debris or dust, undersized for the roof area, or have too few downspouts. Monsoon storms drop large amounts of water quickly. Cleaning before the season and adding downspouts can help.
Why do downspout extensions matter?
Downspout extensions carry water away from your foundation and walls. Without them, water can soak soil next to the house and cause problems. Aim to discharge water several feet away from the home.
Can skylights leak?

Yes, skylights can leak through failed flashing, worn seals or cracked lenses. Condensation can also look like a leak. A roofer can check whether the problem is the skylight itself or the roof around it.
Should I remove an old skylight when replacing my roof?

A roof replacement is a good time to remove, replace or keep a skylight. Old or leaky skylights can be removed and the opening decked over. If you want to keep the light, replacing the skylight during the roof work avoids disturbing the new roof later.
What is a tubular skylight?

A tubular skylight is a small dome on the roof connected to a reflective tube that brings daylight into a room. It requires a smaller roof opening than a traditional skylight. Like any penetration, it needs proper flashing.
What is roof decking?

Roof decking, or sheathing, is the layer of plywood or OSB attached to the roof framing. Underlayment and roofing are installed on top of it. Damaged decking must be replaced so the new roof has a solid base.
What does roof underlayment do?

Underlayment is a water-resistant layer installed over the roof decking and beneath the roofing material. It protects the home from water that gets past the top layer. On tile roofs, the underlayment is the main waterproofing barrier.
What are hips, ridges and valleys on a roof?

A ridge is the top line where two roof slopes meet, and a hip is an outward-facing sloped edge where slopes meet. A valley is the inward angle where two slopes meet and water collects. Each needs specific flashing and roofing details.
What is a roof penetration?

A roof penetration is anything that goes through the roof, such as plumbing vents, exhaust fans, skylights, chimneys and solar mounts. Each penetration needs flashing to keep water out. Penetrations are common leak points.
What is a dead valley on a roof?

A dead valley is an area where water collects because two roof sections or a roof and wall meet without a clear path for drainage. These spots often leak. They need careful flashing and sometimes a cricket to direct water away.
Why do roof vents get damaged?
Plastic roof vents can become brittle in the Arizona sun, and storms can crack or dent them. Their flashing can also fail over time. Damaged vents should be replaced to prevent leaks and pests.
What is a rake edge on a roof?

The rake is the sloped edge of a roof that runs from the eave to the ridge, usually at a gable end. It needs edge flashing or trim to protect against wind and water. On tile roofs, rake tiles cover this edge.
Why do roof-to-wall joints leak?

Roof-to-wall joints leak when step flashing, headwall flashing or counter flashing fails or wasn't installed correctly. Cracked stucco above the joint can also let water in. These joints are common in Arizona homes with multiple rooflines.
What is an eave on a roof?
The eave is the lower edge of the roof that usually overhangs the walls. It helps shed water away from the house and provides shade. Eaves often include vents, bird stops on tile roofs and gutters.

categories.intro: How to reach us, where we work and what to expect.
faqs: How do I contact Integrity Roofing?
Call us at 602-548-3770; phone is the only way to reach us. If we don't answer, leave a message and we'll return your call within 24 hours. We're happy to answer questions and schedule an estimate.
What are Integrity Roofing's office hours?

Our office is open Monday to Friday, 7 am to 5 pm, and closed Saturday and Sunday. Call 602-548-3770 during those hours. If we don't answer, leave a message and we'll return your call within 24 hours.
What happens if I call when your office is closed?

Leave a message with your name, phone number and a short description of your roofing issue. If we don't answer, leave a message and we'll return your call within 24 hours. We don't have a separate line outside office hours.
Where is Integrity Roofing's office?
Our office is at 16308 E Fairview St, Gilbert, AZ 85295. It's our only office. Call 602-548-3770 before stopping by.
What areas does Integrity Roofing serve?

We serve Gilbert, Mesa, Chandler, Queen Creek, San Tan Valley, Tempe, Phoenix, Scottsdale, Apache Junction, Ahwatukee, Glendale and Peoria. If you're near one of these cities, call 602-548-3770 to ask about your location. If we don't answer, leave a message and we'll return your call within 24 hours.
Is Integrity Roofing licensed?
Yes, we're licensed with the Arizona Registrar of Contractors under ROC #096629. We're also bonded and insured. You can verify our license at roc.az.gov.
How long has Integrity Roofing been in business?
We've been family owned and operated since 1993. Over that time we've completed more than 2,500 projects. Learn more on our /about-us/ page.
Is Integrity Roofing a family-owned company?
Yes, Integrity Roofing is family owned and operated. We've served Arizona homeowners and businesses since 1993. Our office is in Gilbert.
What roofing services does Integrity Roofing offer?

We offer roof repairs and maintenance, roof inspections, roof replacement and re-roofing, tile underlayment replacement, and storm and monsoon damage repair. We also install and recoat foam roofs, apply elastomeric coatings and work on flat roofs. We serve both residential and commercial customers.
What roof types does Integrity Roofing work on?

We work on concrete and clay tile, asphalt shingles, spray foam, flat roofs, coated roofs and sloped roofs. If you're not sure what kind of roof you have, describe it when you call. We'll tell you whether it's a roof we work on.
What information should I have ready when I call?

Have your address, the type of roof if you know it, and a short description of the problem or project ready. It also helps to know the roof's approximate age and whether you have an HOA or solar panels. Photos of interior stains or storm damage are useful to have on hand for the estimate visit.
Will I get a written estimate?

Yes, we provide a written estimate that describes the scope of work for your roof. Review it, ask questions and compare it with others before you decide. Ask about financing during the estimate if you'd like to hear the options.
How do I schedule a roofing estimate?

Call us at 602-548-3770 to schedule an estimate. If we don't answer, leave a message and we'll return your call within 24 hours. Every roof is different, so we'll look at yours before giving you a price.
Does Integrity Roofing repair monsoon damage?

Yes, we repair storm and monsoon damage, including displaced tiles, missing shingles, damaged flashing and leaks. Call 602-548-3770 after a storm. If we don't answer, leave a message and we'll return your call within 24 hours.
Does Integrity Roofing work in HOA communities?

Yes, we work in HOA communities across our service area. We can provide the product, manufacturer and color details your architectural committee usually asks for. It's best to start the HOA approval process early.
Does Integrity Roofing serve the West Valley?
Yes, our service area includes Phoenix, Glendale and Peoria. We also serve Scottsdale, Tempe, Ahwatukee and the East Valley. Call 602-548-3770 to schedule.
Does Integrity Roofing serve Queen Creek, San Tan Valley and Apache Junction?
Yes, Queen Creek, San Tan Valley and Apache Junction are all part of our service area. They're close to our Gilbert office. Call 602-548-3770 to schedule an estimate.
Can Integrity Roofing help with my insurance claim?

We can inspect your roof, document storm damage and provide a repair estimate you can share with your insurer. We don't give legal advice or act as a public adjuster. Your insurer decides what your policy covers.
Where can I see Integrity Roofing's past work?
You can see examples of our projects on our /gallery/ page. Customer feedback is on our /reviews/ page. Both give a sense of the work we do across the Valley.
Where can I find more roofing information from Integrity Roofing?

Our /resources/ page and /resources/library/ have more guides for Arizona homeowners. The Roofing Cost Guide at /resources/roofing-cost-guide/ explains what affects roofing prices. You can also call 602-548-3770 with questions.
